label: Charles FCH32 Flex Compact Hub, 4 feed / 32 drop, SC/APC
notes: The 32-drop enclosure the catalogue was missing, and the one a default PON design can call for: engine/design.js ships the ratios 8 / 16 / 32, the catalogue carries plc-1x32-sca and plc-1x32-sca-conn cassettes, and the only splitter box was splitter-box-16 at 17 cable ports - so a 32-drop site (one feeder in, 32 drops out = 33 cables) was 16 cables past the box it was drawn in, and a hand-drawn 1:32 plant read 'over-ported' on the box the site actually is. Figures: Charles Industries Flex Compact Hub (FCH), 32-port enclosure data sheet (CFIT-Flex Compact Hub 32): a swing-out fiber bulkhead with 36 SC/APC fiber adapters, 4 feed and 32 distribution; a backplane that takes up to three small hinged splice trays, each holding a maximum of 24 splices of 900 micron; a 1x32 PLC splitter tray option (CFST-S11320A) mounted on a 4x6 inch splice tray with a 900 micron input stub and SC/APC 900 micron pre-connectorised output pigtails; two bottom cable entry port locations, left and right, each with one 1 inch grommet behind a removable port plate; wall or pole mounting; rugged UL94-5VA polycarbonate, 15 x 12 x 5.5 in (38 x 30.5 x 14 cm), 7 lb (3.18 kg) empty, 216-tool lockable door with padlock hasp; designed to meet GR-950, GR-2898, NEMA 4 and IP66; the applications the sheet names are garden apartments, low-rise MDU, strip malls / FTTB and campuses. What the engine reads, and why the numbers are what they are: `ports` is 36 because that is the sheet's OWN cable count - 4 feed adapters plus 32 distribution adapters, one cable per adapter - and engine/network.js compares the spans touching the node against it, so a full load of 4 feeders plus 32 drops is 36 cables into 36 ports and silent, where a 37th cable is the first one over. The two 1 inch grommet entry plates are where the cables physically enter and are deliberately NOT added on top of the 36: a grommet is a way in, not another way to terminate a fibre, and adding them would count the same cables twice. The 4 feed adapters are why a dual-feeder or cascaded hub is the same row - up to four feeder cables terminate on the bulkhead. Read `ports` as the enclosure's CABLE capacity, not as a drop count: the engine counts cables, so 33 drops into the 32 distribution adapters is 34 cables in 36 ports and draws no port warning - what catches that load is the bulkhead's own 32 adapters, stated here and in the label, not the field the engine reads. `spliceCapacity` is 72 as the empty enclosure (3 trays x 24), not 72 as built: fitting the 1x32 splitter tray spends one of the three trays, so a build that carries the splitter has two trays and about 48 splice positions for the feeder joint, the input stub and any through-fibres - check the tray count before promising a 72-splice through-joint in this box. The splitter tray is pre-terminated on its outputs (SC/APC pigtails) with a 900 micron input stub, which is neither of the catalogue's two 1x32 rows exactly: plc-1x32-sca bills one fusion splice at the input, plc-1x32-sca-conn bills two SC/APC matings for a shelf module's input, and neither bills the 32 output adapters - drop-side connectors are the connector rows charged on the spans. Pick the splitter row that matches how the tray you order terminates its input. `type` is `splitter-box` because that is the function the engine names - a cassette site presenting drop adapters - even though the enclosure is a wall/pole-mounted MDU hub rather than a pad-mount cabinet such as ocsh-288-cabinet. Every figure here is one product data sheet's published capacity, a vendor specification rather than a measured build: replace these figures with the enclosure and splitter tray actually purchased before ordering, and with the as-built splice count once the troughs are closed.
